# Chapter 3: Naming Guidelines — 3.3–3.8

Rules that no analyzer enforces (judgment), CONSIDER rules that analyzers only suggest, and rules that analyzers check only in part, marked "(partly checked)". Open the examples file for the explanation and code the book gives with each rule.

## 3.3 Names of Assemblies, DLLs, and Packages

- **FDG3025** DO choose names for your assembly DLLs that suggest large chunks of functionality, such as `System.Data`. (not in test projects) — examples: examples/ch03-naming-3-3-on.md#fdg3025
- **FDG3026** CONSIDER naming DLLs according to the following pattern: (not in test projects) — examples: examples/ch03-naming-3-3-on.md#fdg3026

## 3.4 Names of Namespaces

- **FDG3027** DO prefix namespace names with a company name to prevent namespaces from different companies from having the same name. (not in test projects) — examples: examples/ch03-naming-3-3-on.md#fdg3027
- **FDG3028** DO use a stable, version-independent product name at the second level of a namespace name. (not in test projects) — examples: examples/ch03-naming-3-3-on.md#fdg3028
- **FDG3029** DO NOT use organizational hierarchies as the basis for names in namespace hierarchies, because group names within corporations tend to be short-lived. Organize the hierarchy of namespaces around groups of related technologies. (not in test projects)
- **FDG3030** DO use PascalCasing, and separate namespace components with periods (e.g., `Microsoft.Office.PowerPoint`). If your brand employs nontraditional casing, you should follow the casing defined by your brand, even if it deviates from normal namespace casing. (partly checked) (not in test projects)
- **FDG3031** CONSIDER using plural namespace names where appropriate. (not in test projects) — examples: examples/ch03-naming-3-3-on.md#fdg3031
- **FDG3032** DO NOT use the same name for a namespace and a type in that namespace. (partly checked) (not in test projects) — examples: examples/ch03-naming-3-3-on.md#fdg3032

## 3.4.1 Namespaces and Type Name Conflicts

- **FDG3033** DO NOT introduce overly general type names such as `Element`, `Node`, `Log`, and `Message`. (partly checked) (not in test projects) — examples: examples/ch03-naming-3-3-on.md#fdg3033

## 3.4.1.1 Application Model Namespaces

- **FDG3034** DO NOT give the same name to multiple types across namespaces within a single application model. (not in test projects) — examples: examples/ch03-naming-3-3-on.md#fdg3034

## 3.4.1.3 Core Namespaces

- **FDG3035** DO NOT give types names that would conflict with any type in the core namespaces. (not in test projects) — examples: examples/ch03-naming-3-3-on.md#fdg3035

## 3.4.1.4 Technology Namespace Groups

- **FDG3036** DO NOT assign type names that would conflict with other types within a single technology. (not in test projects)
- **FDG3037** DO NOT introduce type name conflicts between types in technology namespaces and an application model namespace (unless the technology is not expected to be used with the application model). (not in test projects) — examples: examples/ch03-naming-3-3-on.md#fdg3037

## 3.5 Names of Classes, Structs, and Interfaces

- **FDG3038** DO name classes and structs with nouns or noun phrases, using PascalCasing. (not in test projects) — examples: examples/ch03-naming-3-3-on.md#fdg3038
- **FDG3039** DO name interfaces with adjective phrases, or occasionally with nouns or noun phrases. (not in test projects) — examples: examples/ch03-naming-3-3-on.md#fdg3039
- **FDG3040** DO NOT give class names a prefix (e.g., “C”). (not in test projects) — examples: examples/ch03-naming-3-3-on.md#fdg3040
- **FDG3041** CONSIDER ending the name of derived classes with the name of the base class. (not in test projects) — examples: examples/ch03-naming-3-3-on.md#fdg3041
- **FDG3043** DO ensure that the names differ only by the “I” prefix on the interface name when you are defining a class–interface pair where the class is a standard implementation of the interface. (not in test projects) — examples: examples/ch03-naming-3-3-on.md#fdg3043

## 3.5.1 Names of Generic Type Parameters

- **FDG3044** DO name generic type parameters with descriptive names unless a single-letter name is completely self-explanatory and a descriptive name would not add value. (not in test projects) — examples: examples/ch03-naming-3-3-on.md#fdg3044
- **FDG3045** CONSIDER using `T` as the type parameter name for types with one single-letter type parameter. (not in test projects) — examples: examples/ch03-naming-3-3-on.md#fdg3045
- **FDG3047** CONSIDER indicating constraints placed on a type parameter in the name of the parameter. (not in test projects) — examples: examples/ch03-naming-3-3-on.md#fdg3047

## 3.5.2 Names of Common Types

- **FDG3048** DO follow the guidelines described in Table 3-5 when naming types derived from or implementing certain .NET types. (partly checked) (not in test projects) — examples: examples/ch03-naming-3-3-on.md#fdg3048
- **FDG3050** DO add the suffix “EventHandler” to names of delegates that are used in events. (partly checked) (not in test projects) (context: System.Delegate)
- **FDG3051** DO add the suffix “Callback” to names of delegates other than those used as event handlers. (partly checked) (not in test projects) (context: System.Delegate)
- **FDG3054** DO NOT derive from this class; use the keyword supported by your language instead; for example, in C#, use the `enum` keyword. (not in test projects) (context: System.Enum)
- **FDG3057** DO add the suffix “Dictionary.” Note that `IDictionary` is a specific type of collection, but this guideline takes precedence over the more general collections guideline that follows. (partly checked) (not in test projects) (context: IDictionary IDictionary<TKey, TValue>)
- **FDG3058** DO add the suffix “Collection,” except for reusable, specialized data types such as “Queue” and “HashSet.” (partly checked) (not in test projects) (context: IEnumerable ICollection IList IEnumerable<T> ICollection<T> IList<T>)

## 3.5.3 Naming Enumerations

- **FDG3060** DO use a singular type name for an enumeration unless its values are bit fields. (not in test projects) — examples: examples/ch03-naming-3-3-on.md#fdg3060
- **FDG3061** DO use a plural type name for an enumeration with bit fields as values, also called flags enum. (not in test projects) — examples: examples/ch03-naming-3-3-on.md#fdg3061
- **FDG3064** DO NOT use a prefix on enumeration value names (e.g., “ad” for ADO enums, “rtf” for rich text enums). (partly checked) (not in test projects) — examples: examples/ch03-naming-3-3-on.md#fdg3064

## 3.6.1 Names of Methods

- **FDG3065** DO give methods names that are verbs or verb phrases. (not in test projects) — examples: examples/ch03-naming-3-3-on.md#fdg3065

## 3.6.2 Names of Properties

- **FDG3066** DO name properties using a noun, noun phrase, or adjective. (not in test projects) — examples: examples/ch03-naming-3-3-on.md#fdg3066
- **FDG3068** DO name collection properties with a plural phrase describing the items in the collection instead of using a singular phrase followed by “List” or “Collection.” (partly checked) (not in test projects) — examples: examples/ch03-naming-3-3-on.md#fdg3068
- **FDG3069** DO name Boolean properties with an affirmative phrase (`CanSeek` instead of `CantSeek`). Optionally, you can also prefix Boolean properties with “Is,” “Can,” or “Has,” but only where it adds value. (not in test projects) — examples: examples/ch03-naming-3-3-on.md#fdg3069
- **FDG3070** CONSIDER giving a property the same name as its type. (not in test projects) — examples: examples/ch03-naming-3-3-on.md#fdg3070

## 3.6.3 Names of Events

- **FDG3071** DO name events with a verb or a verb phrase. (not in test projects) — examples: examples/ch03-naming-3-3-on.md#fdg3071
- **FDG3072** DO give events names with a concept of before and after, using the present and past tenses, such as `Closing` and `Closed`. (not in test projects) — examples: examples/ch03-naming-3-3-on.md#fdg3072
- **FDG3073** DO NOT use “Before” or “After” prefixes or postfixes to indicate pre- and post-events. Use present and past tenses as just described. (partly checked) (not in test projects)
- **FDG3074** DO name event handlers (delegates used as types of events) with the “EventHandler” suffix, such as `ClickedEventHandler`. (partly checked) (not in test projects) — examples: examples/ch03-naming-3-3-on.md#fdg3074
- **FDG3075** DO use two parameters named *sender* and *e* in event handlers. (partly checked) (not in test projects) — examples: examples/ch03-naming-3-3-on.md#fdg3075

## 3.6.4 Naming Fields

- **FDG3077** DO use PascalCasing in field names. (partly checked) (not in test projects) — examples: examples/ch03-naming-3-3-on.md#fdg3077
- **FDG3078** DO name fields using a noun, noun phrase, or adjective. (not in test projects)
- **FDG3079** DO NOT use a prefix for `public` or `protected` field names. (partly checked) (not in test projects) — examples: examples/ch03-naming-3-3-on.md#fdg3079

## 3.7 Naming Parameters

- **FDG3080** DO use camelCasing in parameter names. (partly checked) (not in test projects) — examples: examples/ch03-naming-3-3-on.md#fdg3080
- **FDG3081** DO use descriptive parameter names. (not in test projects) — examples: examples/ch03-naming-3-3-on.md#fdg3081
- **FDG3082** CONSIDER using names based on a parameter’s meaning rather than the parameter’s type. (not in test projects) — examples: examples/ch03-naming-3-3-on.md#fdg3082

## 3.7.1 Naming Operator Overload Parameters

- **FDG3083** DO use *left* and *right* for binary operator overload parameter names if there is no meaning to the parameters. (not in test projects) — examples: examples/ch03-naming-3-3-on.md#fdg3083
- **FDG3084** DO use *value* for unary operator overload parameter names if there is no meaning to the parameters. (not in test projects) — examples: examples/ch03-naming-3-3-on.md#fdg3084
- **FDG3085** CONSIDER meaningful names for operator overload parameters if doing so adds significant value. (not in test projects) — examples: examples/ch03-naming-3-3-on.md#fdg3085
- **FDG3086** DO NOT use abbreviations or numeric indices for operator overload parameter names. (partly checked) (not in test projects) — examples: examples/ch03-naming-3-3-on.md#fdg3086

## 3.8 Naming Resources

- **FDG3087** DO NOT directly expose localizable resources as public (or protected) members. (partly checked) (library only) — examples: examples/ch03-naming-3-3-on.md#fdg3087
